advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_writes_to_stdout` fail closed on `file=` targets it cannot prove to be non-stdout (flag, or require a `# js-safe-ok:` sanction) rather than exempting every non-`sys.stdout` name.
evidence: `_callee_name` on an `ast.Name` returns `func.id`, so `file=out` -> "out" -> not in set -> False -> the site is skipped; on `sys.__stdout__` it returns "sys.__stdout__" -> also skipped.

ABSENCE: the gate's stated purpose (docstring lines 37-45) is to catch a FUTURE emitter reintroducing the direct construct, so an unresolved/aliased `file=` target that IS stdout at runtime is precisely the case that must not fail open.
advisory.finding: `_writes_to_stdout` treats a `print(..., file=X)` as off-stdout for ANY `X` whose lexical callee name is not exactly `sys.stdout`/`stdout`. A `file=` target that resolves to stdout at runtime — a variable bound to `sys.stdout` (`file=out`), `file=sys.__stdout__`, or any handle the checker can't statically name — is silently exempted, so a future `print(json.dumps(doc), file=<stdout-alias>)` puts a raw big-int on the wire yet yields no violation, indistinguishable from a clean file.
advisory.suggested_fix: Only exempt an explicit KNOWN-stderr/non-stdout target (e.g. `file=sys.stderr`); for a `file=` value that is not statically recognizable as stdout AND not a known off-stdout handle, still flag it (or treat unresolved names conservatively as stdout) so the negative verdict cannot mask an aliased-stdout write.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test pinning the intended verdict for `print(json.dumps(doc), file=<non-literal handle>)` (an aliased/unresolved `file=` target).
evidence: ABSENCE: no case exercises `print(json.dumps(doc), file=out)` / `file=sys.__stdout__` where the target is unresolved or a stdout alias — the exact escape the `file=` whitelist opens.

Rejected table only adds `"import sys, json\nprint(json.dumps(doc), file=sys.stdout)\n"` (test_cli_json_js_safe_guard.py:75) — the dotted form; no `from sys import stdout; print(..., file=stdout)` case

Named violating input the added lines would mishandle under a set regression: `import json
from sys import stdout
print(json.dumps(doc), file=stdout)
` (should be flagged, currently untested)
advisory.finding: The new scoping/exemption behavior is untested for an ambiguous `file=` target: tests cover only `file=sys.stdout` (rejected) and `file=sys.stderr` (allowed), leaving the widened exemption for `file=<variable/alias>` (which currently passes silently) without regression coverage.
merged_from: The newly added `_STDOUT_FILE_TARGETS = {"sys.stdout", "stdout"}` set has a `"stdout"` (bare-alias) branch that no test exercises: only the dotted `file=sys.stdout` form is tested. A `print(json.dumps(doc), file=stdout)` (with `from sys import stdout`) must be flagged, mirroring the existing `bare-stdout-write` rejection case, but that path is untested — a regression collapsing the set to just `{"sys.stdout"}` would pass all tests.
